item.title: The chamber of eternity
item.description: EMERGENCY MEETING !!!!!!!!!!!
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): Regular SCP page, with Containment Procedures, Descriptions, And addendums

Elevator Pitch: A Chamber is found off the coast of Great Britain covered in strange runes the Foundation can't translate. This chamber allows for short-distance multiversal travel, connecting to around 4 other universes. One person is required to link themselves to this chamber, and then other instances of them can travel through into the present reality. Fondation uses this to connect to other Foundation's, and using their information to collect anomalies before they become an issue.

Central Narrative:

+ Yesyes click on me
- Here you go !!!!!

A junior researcher with a strong background in multiversal studies is selected to link themself to this chamber, by entering inside and connecting them self to other versions of themself. Other foundation instances of this junior researcher come through, and they provide valuable insight into the several SCP's this reality did not possess. The other instances include
1. A site director.
2. a very high ranking officer in the foundation's military division, and is in far better shape then the main junior researcher,
3. Still a junior scientist, but from a universe where the Foundation is on great diplomatic terms with the Wanderer's Library, so this version has various thaumaturgic capabilities.
4. The only one is not a foundation member, but is an avid Parawatch user, and her insight is useful enough to keep around, albeit with the caveat that she will be amentisied before returning to her home plane.
Over time, The main junior researcher reports a decreased emotionally stability, and requests various times to be released from the project, citing "These other versions of me are way smarter and i'm just a burden on studying this project." His requests are not given. All signs point to the main version of this researcher snapping, and then the version that isn't a foundation member is shown trying to take out the one with the thaumaturgy, which obviously doesn't go well. Using the help of the other versions translate's the runes to say "May your strong leaders enter, and the strongest leader exit.”

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The containment procedures will mention how SCP-XXXX-1 goes through several physiological evaluations through out the course of the chamber being active, and different versions of themself are to be kept apart. They will be written to show a lot of precaution for a
Thaumiel object.

Additional Notes: The ancient group that created this object will be present in every alternative reality, but not the main one. This chamber was used by the king’s of this country to prove they were the strongest possible version of themselves.

item.title: Idea Critique: Staff conflicted morals on a anomalous site.
item.description: SCP Idea about conflicting morals for foundation staff.
item.content:encoded:
Greenlight Status: Seeking

Page Type: SCP Document (and accompanying tale about prison break after greenlight)

Premise: The premise is about an anomalous village filled with people (SCP-XXXX-1 or -1s) that are generally harmless inside, but if they get out they could be dangerous (how they are dangerous is to be determined, but not world-ending - maybe just dangerous to the civilian populace). The staff are instructed to not sympathize, but are not told what will happen if they do.

Hook: The catch and twist of the story is how the staff fight each other from the ones who want to let the -1s out, and the ones who want to keep them contained. There will probably be a separate tale about both sides of the conflict if this is greenlighted.

Basically about conflicting morals for foundation staff, and who is the "bad guy" - letting the -1s out, or keeping them contained.

item.title: Scandinavians, look here! - The Scandinavian Branch (ND) seeks recruits!
item.description: Recruitment thread for the Scandinavian Branch (ND).
item.content:encoded:
Hello!

We in the Scandinavian branch (ND) of the SCP Foundation are looking for new members. If you happen to speak Danish, Norwegian, Swedish, or even Faroese, you are more than welcome to come join the ND Wiki and the ND Discord server!

Because the ND branch is still in need of further development, we're especially interested in people with experience in any of the following areas:
- Moderation and Administration
- CSS coding and other technical know-how
- Translation
- Creative writing in Danish, Faroese, Norwegian, and/or Swedish

If you have experience in the two first areas (in addition to speaking one of the four languages) and wish to apply that knowledge in ND, please contact me directly with a short resume of your experiences.

Of course you're welcome as a member even if you don't already have a background in any of these areas. We need all the help we can get.
So if you're interested, come on over to http://scp-nd.wikidot.com/ and sign up!
You're also welcome to join our Discord server at: https://discord.gg/QTsMfgAu

item.title: The Goddess Fertility Engine
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article and subsequent Tale if more information is requested

Page Layout: The article will open by stating the containment of the SCP is of high importance, but failure to capture will not result in consequences beyond the lack of benefits of the SCP.

Elevator Pitch: The SCP is a machine of unknown and anomalous origin which houses an apparatus to restrain a human woman. Once inside this apparatus the machine’s anamolous properties take affect and give the human woman increased size as well as reality altering abilities. The machine appears only in the result of a K-class event, and the foundation is unsure whether it causes such events, or is guaranteed to appear in every instance of a K-class event or only certain varieties. The woman inside the machine is basically a “goddess” although in a very loose sense, capable of reproduction without a male counterpart, as well as a variety of properties that allow the woman to manipulate matter, environments, weather etc. It appears acts as a sort of life engine for a new world once the earth is inhabitable.
Central Narrative: The narrative centers around the foundations lack of knowledge of its capabilities, and if containment or capture would even cause harm to the earth itself. The foundation only knows about the machine and the transformation process through the reports from SCP-507, and through numerous different exposures and sightings from 507 more information is revealed, although much of the process is still mysterious, leading to the foundation drawing conclusions and pour resources into claiming the machine.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
I think the vagueness of the scp makes it interesting. It’s one of those items that the foundation knows it must contain due to the value of such machinery, while at the same time not even quite understanding what the machine even is other than a possible fresh start for man kind.

Additional Notes:
This is a very rough explanation. I have a draft worked out already but don’t know how to explain it in the short length of 400 words. Thanks for taking your time to read my draft!

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) The Ancient Gateway
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights:** Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror/Comedy

Elevator Pitch: An ancient interdimensional gateway with an unknown origin located somewhere in the underground of the North Pole, which leads to a world where lies a cosmic entity whose claimed to be a being that has existed longer than existence itself, however, with the mind of a kind-hearted average joe.

Central Narrative:

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-XXXX appears to be an ancient gateway with an unknown origin. The gateway is approximately 8,849 meters constructed out of unknown solid materialize and has unknown symbols are written all over it. Any individual who walks into SCP-XXXX would lead them to a realm, where an entity whose size is inapplicably being held. The anomaly is designated as SCP-XXXX-01. SCP-XXXX-01 appears to be an inorganic entity with no human facial features, no signs of hair, eyes, nose, mouth, or eyes. Its body has entirely different physiology that is presumed to be a non-existent type.

SCP-XXXX-01 shows no signs of hostility is capable of speech, shown to have unique knowledge. It would be able to remain patiently/motionless in one place without feeling any urges/aggression over many years1. However, sometimes it would leave its place2, and will not feel disturbed if any individuals are there to observe it.

SCP-XXXX was first discovered when a group of individuals who are exploring the North Pole has reported to the authorities that they'd discovered it after finding a passage that leads deep down to its location while in the middle of finding shelter to avoid an upcoming snowstorm. As this was brought to the Foundation, they've covered it up as fast as possible and deployed a group of agents, MTF-Twilight-10, codename "Broken Stellers," was deployed with the duty is to accompany all of the witnesses out and monitor/guard the area.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP was inspired by a powerful "god" who is actually a powerful cosmic being named Venrensorys. But with a few aspects added and some changes.

Additional Notes: So, after watching through SCP-2662, I've decided to come up with this idea.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn
Footnotes
1. Stated in the interview, it can wait patiently for even eternities.
2. Stated in the interview.

item.title: SCP concept-The ring of mimicry
item.description: A ring that turns its container into a hostile object
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: its a simple ring that when stored in a container for a given time, it will transform that object into a mimic until taken out. Its containment procedures prevent mimicry by moving it between boxes frequently.

Central Narrative: The ring, while easy to contain, can be catastrophic if not watched after. It does not have a size limit on what it can animate. That means, if given time, the ring could animate the entire facility (key word is given time, it would take decades for the ring to achieve that). Thus the ring has many re-containment procedures and fail-safes to prevent that.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: For this idea, I tried to turn the whole box idea on its head. The whole "if you put it in a box and it stays there, then its safe", I thought about if you put it in a box and then the box tried to kill you, what would it be?

Additional Notes: This is my second idea for an SCP, I'm still very new to this so my clinical tone and ideas may not be satisfactory, I'm open to all critique as I'm here purely to improve.

item.title: City of normacy
item.description: Nothing anomalous here.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Two standard SCP pages, one outdated for the zone with its discovery and test logs and one for the anomalous human.

Elevator Pitch: The Foundations discovers an area that negates anomalous effects and memories or instructions relating to the anomalous, making them try a more indirect approach to learn about the anomaly which would lead to them to discover that it is caused unknowingly by a human with interest in the supernatural.

Central Narrative: The Foundation discovers an area capable of overriding any anomalous effect, records, or memories related to anomalies or groups of interest after they lose contact with an operative who had remained in the area and find him days later with no memories of his mission or any event related to the Foundation. When investigating the area, other operatives and equipment end up being affected, at which point the Foundation makes the first designation and prepares to investigate in greater depth only to find that all orders or influence are lost in the area, preventing the evacuation of the city ​​or direct communication with its inhabitants while they are inside; limiting himself to observing the area from afar, interviewing anyone leaving the city and determining the boundaries of the area.
During the course of the investigation, the Foundation determines the limits of this anomaly, noting that it varies its position with the passage of time but always maintains the same size, which ends up revealing the person to whom the area is connected. Due to the restrictions given by the anomaly, the Foundation uses his online presence, records, and surveillance to learn about the SCP, discovering his interest in the supernatural.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The research on the limits of the anomaly through unusual means by the Foundation and the discovery of the human cause and its implications.

Additional Notes: I want some advice on how to make the most of the build-up to finish up the article.

item.title: The Maw
item.description: A solar system consumed by a parasitic biomass that spans planets and stars.
item.content:encoded:
I understand that new authors typically don't write Keter-class scips, but this one just stuck with me, so here I am.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP article

Genre: Mystery, Horror, Action with hints of desperation

Page Layout: Standard format (no ACS)

Elevator Pitch: A solar system that is roughly 2000 Au1 in diameter which is overtaken by a biomass of tremendous proportions. Said biomass is a colonial organism with organic linkages that span the distances between celestial bodies and envelop the planets themselves, effectively turning the entire system into a breeding ground for smaller units of the organism, thus furthering its reach. A central mass which measures ~1.92 million km in diameter engulfs the system's sun, and a large, ovular maw sits atop it.

+Brace Yourself
-You need more time to brace?

[This maw ejects chitinous pods (SCP-XXXX-2) containing small, wormlike entities measuring 45 cm in length (SCP-XXXX-2-A). These pods will crash within a 2 km radius of the coordinates 84"37'02"S 68"32'55"E (Antarctica). Approximately one (1) hour after landing, these worms will "hatch" and burrow into the ice. It is shown that organisms proceed to grow at an indeterminate rate while in these conditions.

When exposed to a human being, SCP-XXXX-2-A will merge with the human's spinal column, controlling synapses and effectively taking the subject over. These instances are aggressive to all forms of life and show resistance to pain. Due to this outcome, a mobile task force (Hammer Down, maybe?) will be stationed within this two kilometer zone, and the trajectories of SCP-XXXX-2 will be tracked. Upon finding the crash zone, MTF will destroy SCP-XXXX-2 and SCP-XXXX-2-A by several means (I've written up a list of these means that will be in the official article.)

The final section of this SCP (I promise), referred to as SCP-XXXX-3, is a triangular portal with equa-distant sides that measures 15 meters tall, located at 84"37'02"S 68"32'55"E. It transports anyone entering to a corresponding portal within SCP-XXXX-1 (the solar system).
]

SCP-XXXX-1 and SCP-XXXX-3 were destroyed by MTF during an exploration, thus re-classifying SCP-XXXX as neutralized.

Central Narrative: The article contains a few exploration logs, which culminates with an MTF force detonating a large device that cause the star to implode, eviscerating all components of the SCP.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Several, the first of which will be the title and the "Keter Neutralized" classification. An image too, if I can find one or make my own.

Additional Notes: I was reading a bit about making first time Scips too complex/long. I fully intend to be as concise as possible (no 1730 here, folks). It might also be a bright idea for the struck-through class to be Keter-alterius, due to its alien origins.

Footnotes
1. [The standard unit of measurement used to delineate extremely large distances]

item.title: A SCP idea I have
item.description: A dummy that makes people go insane.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror and mystery

Page Layout (Optional): The standard SCP article format.

Elevator Pitch: The basic idea is a jointed 2 metre tall dummy made of hardwood. When someone views it directly, the person will begin to have visual hallucinations centered around the dummy, This usually drives the viewer to the point of insanity which almost always results in suicide. This is one of 2 methods of killing its victim. The alternative and less likely way of killing is directly attacking its victim, Its theorized that it does this by blurring the vision of any nearby person and/or recording devices that may witness this event. This method is only used when the first does not work.
The entity is capable of controlling nearby lights and electronics, which allows the anomaly to speak in morse code. Recent interviews have gathered that the entity came from, in its words "World human not know" implying that it came from an alternate reality. It also states "other came with" what this means is unknown.
Central Narrative: The entity was found inside of an abandoned factory with unknown origins in 2006, after many people complained about seeing a "wooden thing" watching them from inside the factory. Paranormal investigators found this interesting and went inside, they went missing a few days later, they were found dead in their homes. Foundation researchers went on the case and successfully captured it, with the cost of more than half of the researchers involved die in their offices. The dummy appears to have been made in the 19th century, a torn-up tag can be seen on the back of the dummy which says "cooperative inc."

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The article will be short and simple, it won't have too much information about the entity leaving a mystery, I am also hoping to add a feeling of dread.

Additional Notes: None.

item.title: What is Love?
item.description: Baby don't hurt me, don't hurt me, no more
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Drama, History

Elevator Pitch: A demonic, non-corporeal entity formerly of divine origin that turned on humanity following a failed GOC neutralization attempt in the 1960s. The entity has limited control over the collective human psyche and has been worshipped by various ancient civilizations as a deity associated with love (Cupid/Eros, Bastet, Freyja, etc). After its fall, it began inflicting deleterious effects on the collective human unconsciousness most clearly observable in secular societies that could gradually lead to an IK-Class Collapse of Global Civilization Scenario if left unchecked. Symptoms include declining birth and marriage rates, increasing divorce and abortion rates, anxiety, low self-esteem, suicidal tendencies, and family breakdowns.

Central Narrative: A joint operation by the GOC, Foundation, and a handful of Serpent's Hand defectors led to the creation of the "Valentia Protocol", which trapped themselves and the entity in a stalemate. It's fueled by people's faith in love, which it actively works to destroy. If the Foundation does nothing it would destroy itself but with disastrous repercussions on the human psyche. By keeping it alive they can mitigate the risk to mankind but are likely only prolonging the inevitable. The primary goal is to buy enough time to find a permanent solution to its elaborate murder-suicide attempt.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The "Valentia Protocol" reveals that the proliferation and spread of Valentine's Day throughout the global community since the late 20th century is a Foundation psyop to counteract its effects. Despite displaying moderate success, this is only a temporary solution until the entity can be appeased, contained, or properly neutralized. Direct manipulation of the collective unconsciousness could have been utilized as a potential workaround if not for the obvious ethical implications as well as all research regarding this endeavor having been (allegedly) destroyed following the SCP-5000 incident.

item.title: My SCP idea
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): I'm not exactly sure but it could fall under mystery I suppose.

Page Layout (Optional): Just a normal set up as this is my first article

Elevator Pitch: There are four parts to this SCPs

  1. A diamond ring in a small black box that when near you gives you weird dreams, all of the dreams have red plecos in them.
  2. A girl that is summoned when the diamond touches any object outside of the box. She will take on one trait from the item.
  3. An alternate universe where all of mankind has been wiped out.
  4. Large red plecos that are highly dangerous in the AU but laughably weak in the main universe.

Central Narrative: A man working for the Foundation would buy his girlfriend a ring in hopes of proposing to her. He would keep the ring with him for a few nights beforehand and would begin having weird dreams. After one of the dreams he would take out the ring and it would drop to his pillow. This would cause the girl to appear. He quickly reported this and the ring was taken and the girl was locked up. A few interviews were done but she was mostly too scared to speak, after 24 hours she disappeared. They would try to get her to come back and would find out that the ring has a cooldown of 12 hours.

+ show block
– hide block

They would bring her back and interview her. They would find out that she was from a universe that was destroyed by beings she would call the "Blood Fish". They would ask her what these blood fish are and she would describe a common pleco but much larger and red. Later they would try to send a camera with her when she goes back to her universe. The camera would be destroyed and she would be sent back to the AU. Next time they would try to send a D-Class. The D-Class would begin to drain blood until all his blood has drained from his body and it is on the ground, killing him. Then one for the blood fish would appear, it would only be a foot long and would just start flopping in the blood. It would be placed in a fish tank where it would act like a normal fish. The girl would freak out during this before being teleported back. In later interviews, it would be shown that in the AU people began to use the blood of animals to replace water after a ton of large red fish began to appear in the rivers. No one seemed harmed by the blood until one day the fish began to float, then all but five people, who were able to resist the urge to consume blood, found five rings that would be able to fight off the fish. They failed and the fish killed all but one, the girl in this article. She was able to hide and due to the main universe's version of her ring being bought she was able to bond herself with that ring so that she can survive.

+ Show
- Hide

• disappearances across arctic and polar regions have been tracked, dating back years, connected to high power storms in said regions
• team is dispatched in front of high-powered storm, isolated from settlements (team receded incident in full)

• a king appeared and stopped above them, waving them to join
• In the forest below the king can be seen a glow and the team walk off towards it.
• the storm returns soon after with the team listed as MIA
• second test involved a D-class with eyewear to counter any magic effect on D-class
• same as before the Wild Hunt appears running along the aroura in the same direction of the storm.
• the king appears and states he is insulted a peasant would not bow before their king
• the D-class proceeds to use a large amount of profanity against the king for calling him a peasant
• the king shouted is anger at the D-class with a thunderous boom and pointed his weapon at the D-class
• in the tree line a number of large hounds with white fur and red tipped ears can be seen appearing along with two knights on skeletal steeds with rusted horse armour and mounted knights with equally worn armour. both rider and horse had a glowing blue mist from their eye sockets/helmet
• the D-class is seen running away with the camera trampled in pursuit
• partial remains were recovered of D-class.
• third attempt involved a rouge scientist utilising same glasses but bowed when the storm broke and the aroura appeared
• the king appeared and welcomed him to rise and join the Hunt with the scientist humbly requesting the king to remain, stating he is the only one left to care for his household

• according to the king he in services of the 'One True God' who beckoned him as a great hunter and leader of men to undertake an Eternal hunt and protect the realm of man from the greatest of threats (no proof at time)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The Mythology of the Wild Hunt, their purpose and the containment procedures. since a storm cannot be contained the foundation use entertainment media (online flash sales of media/ games, putting popular shows on tv, using media to exaggerate severity of storm). those outside during the storms are written off as casualties of the storm.

James Devillian Twist is a reality-penetrating intruder. Having been forcefully injected into this reality from outside its space-time continuum, by his mere existence, however temporary it may be, destiny’s hand has been stabbed.

A key, integral part of this SCP article lies in the interviews and experimentations that take place on him. The story is about discovery and how much information can actually be obtained with the obstacle of the LLUN aura.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
A man named Jack is running for his life in a big city, crying out for help. Upon someone reaching Jack and trying to calm him down, Jack will see Twist appear out of nowhere. Jack panics and flees. The person who would try to help Jack turns to see Devillian.
Regardless of what that person chooses to do, Devillian will continue onward until Jack has been successfully eliminated. Devillian will then vanish without a trace. After a random set period of time, Jack will reappear somewhere else and start running and begging for help. Devillian will appear soon after to kill him. Enter the SCP Foundation.

After trying and failing to save Jack from Twist, the SCP agents will be surprised to see that Devillian decides to willingly go with the SCP agents instead of vanishing into thin air. The real story begins from there.

Additional Notes:
This will be my very first SCP project attempt. I would very much like to know of any particular SCP stories that do anything similar so that I can make sure to further tweak my story into something more unique. My intention will be to have cross scp testing/experimentation with this SCP, not necessarily for anything combat related (though that will come up) but for information gathering purposes. item.title: Cognation : AKA The Ballad of King Robert
item.description: Blood from an empty universe that is used as a 'Hume Sink'
item.content:encoded:
Blood from an empty universe that is used as a 'Hume Sink' within mass produced SRAs holds secrets of beginning and endings.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Mystery/Horror

Page Layout: Standard article layout followed by addendums explaining the scp history/discovery. Then several addendums explaining an incident that occurred. E.I footage transcript, post interview, still image from footage (which I have currently already made). Followed by a final update.

Elevator Pitch:

  • A delve into Reality Anchor Construction and Design
  • An Thamiel anomalous SRA Component with strict rules about thinking about; the colour red, wives, or the fear of blood.
  • Additional component used in SRAs being lobotomized reality benders from Project Ichabod.
  • Robert Scranton implicated to be the source of this blood.
  • The more they feed him reality the stronger he’s becoming.
+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The blood has been used in SRAs to suck excess Hume into an empty universe for a number of years. Foundation first acquires it from testing with flawed wormholes. After some time the acquisition of the blood reveals an advanced state of the blood with hostile telepathic properties and causes a redacted effect when exposed to the body and is constantly drawing humes into the dimension. A researcher goes rogue sending a drone into the origin dimension. Causes a large amount of blood to be converted into the advanced counterpart. Researcher has a tell-all interview with an O5 revealing what and who is the source of the blood. The drone footage analysed and is shown. The blood's conversion is now happening at an increasing rate and will convert all amounts by 20—. O5 Command reclassifying the blood to Keter is pending.

Hook/Attention Grabber: The idea that what if Robert Scranton was the source of this SRA component, the excess humes painfully funneling into the non-dimension, changing the doctor. Turning him into a weak god in the darkness of the abyss, feeding on other gods and becoming hateful of existence itself. A red king in a red reality. Basically what if the Scarlet King is a forgotten echo of a man forced to live and become a god, losing all but his attention on his wife, his bride? Could Robert Scranton’s ending be the Scarlet King’s beginning?

Additional Notes: Idea comes from the similarities of the beginning of Dust and Blood and the ending of SCP-3001. In fact Dr Scranton himself proclaims to be "King Robert" and calls 3001: "My prison. My kingdom all my own," in the article itself. Among a number of interesting coincidences between the two.

item.title: Brain Coral
item.description: A species of parasitic deep sea coral which utilizes a potent cognitohazard as a defense mechanism. The source of all foundation-utilized memetic kill agents.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Conventional, with containment procedures and description followed by supplemental incident reports and experimental logs. This is followed by a "secret" file with restricted access.

Elevator Pitch: The source of all memetic kill agents used by the foundation, as well as the means of inoculation. A species of coral emits a cognitohazardous vibration that forces cardiac arrest in observers. This vibration remains hazardous in any data form. Polyps separate from the coral and enter an animal's brain, whereupon it becomes immune to the cognitohazard. All high ranking officials of the Foundation are hosting a brain parasite. This coral has formed a symbiotic relationship with the entire foundation. This means YOU have the parasite if you've ever survived the SCP-001 kill agent.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The unique effects of the cognitohazard vibration are discovered when security workers are killed viewing the waveform of security footage. Research into its properties and the extent of this effect is undergone. At some point, the idea to use it for security was proposed by the heads of research, Dr. Berryman and Langford, and publicly denied. Shortly after, an "incident" on-site causes the "death" of all coral bushes. In reality, they are quietly moved to an unknown location to implement the memetic security agent.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: My idea is that the true nature of the SCP is hinted at throughout the text before being revealed at the end. The Neutralized classification and description of its supposed destruction should hopefully be somewhat intriguing.

Additional Notes: No idea if this conflicts with any previous articles. As this is my first work and it attempts to retcon something so iconic it may be controversial.

The idea is that the coral will only infect animals that choose not to feed on it, and releases a vibration pulse that travels far underwater and kills all others. This poses the question of what benefit the coral would receive from not simply killing everything around it. Maybe by "whitelisting" certain animals, it can manipulate its ecosystem to evolve beneficially.

Also not sure how the parasite would get in your brain. It would need to enter in a way as to not cause long-term damage if any at all.

SCP-3000 has proven that the Foundation will utilize anomalies to their benefit, although that is arguably less extreme.

This SCP refers collectively to an entire species of coral. Each colony possesses a unique cognitohazardous vibration which can only be prevented by hosting of a polyp from the corresponding colony.

item.title: Festive Jello Strikes Back
item.description: A predatory cognitohazard visually perceived as a plate of Christmas jello.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery, Horror

Elevator Pitch: A seemingly innocent plate of Christmas gelatin (Festive season!), through further analysis, has been determined to be a cognitohazard employed by a gelatinous anomaly. It is able to detect prey by secreting pheromones into the air that when inhaled, awakens a predatory instinct within the gelatinous mass to envelop and consume affected prey item within a 5-meter radius of the plate.

Central Narrative: Field Agents dispatched to investigate an unexplained suburban disappearance of an entire family fails to report to Command. Ergo, an MTF team is deployed to follow up the disappearance, discovering human remains contained inside a mass of layered Christmas jello of an unknown origin. The object is retrieved and returned to an SCP Site wherein it is contained and the Foundation proceeds to conduct testing on the anomaly and gain additional understanding of its anomalous properties for optimal containment procedures.

+ show block
– hide block

After the SCP is confirmed a cognitohazard, it is suspected that the SCP was manufactured by a hitherto unknown Group of Interest. The Foundation launches a wider investigation into the origin of the SCP, sending Field Agents to return to the abandoned suburban home where it was originally discovered. The exploration log indicates that the agent discovers the original packaging and after finding out the brand name, another subsequent investigation reveals the identity of the Group of Interest that managed to evade Foundation radar up to this incident. The story ends with a footnote that ongoing surveillance and monitoring of the G.O.I is underway in order to assess the threat level of the parent G.O.I and ultimately deem whether Foundation intervention is necessary.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The hook starts with the mysterious disappearance of Foundation Field Agents in a peaceful suburban area with no record of kidnapping, homicides or break and entry crimes. This leads to the discovery of the SCP (Through an exploration log). Then the SCP Foundation attempts to understand the SCP's unknown properties (Experimentation log), allowing effective containment to be achieved. The SCP Foundation reasons from its nature as a cognitohazard that there was a strong possibility that the SCP was artificially engineered. The audience is constantly kept engaged by a linear narrative starting off with mystery that later unfolds into a deeper investigation of the SCP's origins.

Additional Notes: Have yet to determine a name for the G.O.I responsible for the manufacturing of the SCP, and have not yet decided whether the G.O.I are a belligerent or benevolent organisation.

item.title: June the 31st
item.description: The Day No One Remembers.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): ACS

Elevator Pitch: This SCP is both the day of June the 31st and the global event that occurs on that day. During the day, members of the public appear to be in a state of complete wholeness and engage in unorthodox, but not unnatural activities. These activities can range from having a picnic in the park, gardening, napping in a graveyard to hugging and weeping. Knowledge of the day appears to be instinctive. People seem to remember it the moment the day begins and steadily forget about it when it finishes1. It also appears that those working for or associated with the Foundation are exempt from this event and are able to remember the happenings of the day. They also don't feel the state of wholeness that the general public experience on the day.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: Something is in the air. Like an uncanny calm. Almost as if the whole world had sighed with relief and tranquility.

The overall story of this SCP is the strange, tranquil state the world enters on June the 31st, the day no-one will remember. Throughout the day, people enter a mindset they will rarely enter on any other day. Everyone is truly occupying their lives. That is, everyone except those in the Foundation, as they appear to be exempt from the SCP's effect. This is further emphasised when Foundation researchers interview people during the SCP. The interviewee treats foundation staff with slight pity and compassion, as if the Foundation is a child who doesn't understand something.

It's suggested that the SCP is necessary in some way. During one experiment, people were subjected to a strong narcotic and skipped the day entirely. Upon waking up, the subject appeared distant, mournful and depressive and continued in this state throughout their lives. It would appear that this SCP maintains a kind of wellbeing inside humanity.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: What I'm really trying to get across is both a feeling of calm peace experienced by the public and a sort of sad envy and exclusion experienced by the Foundation Staff. I haven't seen an SCP which does something beautiful and emphasises the loss Foundation Staff experience when they join the Foundation.

Footnotes
1. This is demonstrated through interviews and experiments.

item.title: Roland The Headless Thompson Gunner
item.description: Yes, inspired by the Warren Zevon song.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Character-Driven, Weird, Action

Elevator Pitch: Tales of vengeance-seeking headless specters have been around for awhile, but there's one that goes underappreciated: Roland the Headless Thompson Gunner, from the song of the same name by Warren Zevon. It seemed like the perfect fuel for an SCP, especially combined with my affinity for weird, character-driven stories.

Central Narrative: The headless spirit of a betrayed mercenary from the first Congo war still roams the earth, seeking out his killer. All the while the Foundation attempts to track him down and put a lock on him as he gets closer to his goal, told through incident logs. Eventually the Foundation finds Roland's killer and brings him in, only for Roland to eventually get in and put an end to him, after which he "shuts down", so the Foundation can easily cram him in a room.
Time passes with the headless gunner just standing there motionless, with several attempts being made to speak to him and see if he's at all aware of his dead state (to no response). Things stay like this until several undercover Chaos Insurgency agents make their move, turning against their Foundation "co-workers". However, even if he couldn't respond, Roland still heard those sessions, and it got him thinking. The being that once fought for money, then for his own revenge, has been awakened again by the cruel betrayal happening in close proximity, and now shall fight for others. One last action scene/log, before Roland vanishes off into the night, his muzzle-flashes illuminating traitor's deeds all around the world.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Roland's killer is initially listed as a POI, and right off the bat in conprocs personnel are advised to immediately report any possible information or leads on who he is, to stop the anomaly's manifestations. From there the procedures list out the types of places prone to getting Roland'ed and weaves a tale of a maniacal globetrotting chase across the seedy underbelly of the world.

Additional Notes: The original song can be found here: https://youtu.be/wRWCK9zGynA
Also, in a funny twist the Foundation winds up getting the tip on where to find Roland's killer from the UIU of all places, as in the song it is stated that Roland's initial killing was ordered by the CIA.

Any and all feedback is greatly appreciated!

item.title: SCP Idea - Algernon-13
item.description: A distant star, when viewed, enhances the viewer's "attributes" based upon what they define themselves as
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Sci-fi, Light horror

Elevator Pitch: A dim, distant star is discovered by a group of astronomers who discover that, when extensively gazed upon, said star can temporarily impart seemingly supernatural enhancements to the viewer. Said enhancements come at a price, however.

Central Narrative: A small research team in Argentina discovers a hitherto unknown star. The initial astronomer who extensively gazes at the star notes a small mote of light in the corner of his eye, though the light dissipates after several hours, since he chooses to ignore it. His partner, however, continues to be bothered by the light in the corner of her eye and keeps staring at it. Once she stares at it for an arbitrary amount of time, she suddenly seizes a marker and begins scribbling strange symbols on a whiteboard. This fit lasts for approximately thirteen hours before she collapses from exhaustion. When she reawakens, she realizes that her knowledge of mathematics and science has been dramatically reduced to roughly that of a first-grade level.

SCP is made aware of this development and has its own team investigate the star, which has been designated Algernon-13 (after the novel "Flowers for Algernon"). Numerous personnel undergo tests, including a former soldier (who experiences increased aggression and muscle growth), a linguist (who briefly becomes an onmiglot), and an artist (who paints gorgeous pictures unlike any she'd ever made before, and which offers some insight into the nature of the star), all of whom suffer severe degradation of their enhanced abilities (i.e. the soldier experiencing muscle atrophy) after thirteen hours have passed. It also becomes apparent that the star is attempting to communicate in some way, and the SCP would detail their efforts to figure out what the star wants.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The hook involves the mystery behind why the star induces "attribute enhancements" on its viewers. The mystery reaches its zenith with the pictures painted by the artist, as they give a nebulous picture of what's going on around the star, leaving one with as many new questions as answers.

Additional Notes: Not sure what to rate this anomaly - Euclid or Keter class. Suggestions would be helpful.

item.title: Rainbow Spray

Similar to SCP-294, it generates scents that the user specifies on a small keyboard under the spray. However, it is still unknown how it can have such power. If I would type say; Blueberry Pie, then the spray would then generate that scent after the user squeezes on it, causing the specific aroma to rise. he locker in which the object resides in is always tested for strange activities. Following that effects discovered so far is mildly damaging to the entity. Once the object is operated 10 times, it will enter into a stage of self-termination, and will decompose into soapy water. There are no effects on the living being however.

Central Narrative: The spray would originally unraveled in a Home Depot. Prior to being discovered, it would be transported to the closest foundation site where it will stay in a locker. For the first few days, the entity would be tested by researchers. Considering the positive uses it maintains, it would be useful for researchers to use it in experiments involving scents.

Additional Notes: Keep in mind that I haven't been on the SCP community for quite a while, so mistakes can occur.

item.title: The Lightswitch
item.description: Just a simple lightswitch that turns YOU off and on. Probably.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Brief SCP article with most content being in Addendum

Elevator Pitch: A lightswitch that, when flicked on, gives the user life and, when flicked off, takes the user’s life. Things get more interesting when living creatures turn it on and dead creatures turn it off.

Central Narrative: The SCP is simple enough; if you flick it off, it takes your consciousness, rendering you essentially dead/vegetative. If someone forces your corpse/vegetative body to flick it on again, you gain your consciousness back.

Collapsed for mobile users
Collapsed for mobile users

However, if somebody who is alive flicks it on, they absorb the consciousness of the person who flicked it off. This forces two minds to share one body. Although the original host is mostly in control, absorbed consciousness are capable of forcing actions with enough concentration. This will require them to overwhelm the original host, which can be extremely difficult, especially if the host was specifically trained for mental fortitude/self-control. The host can choose to read other consciousnesses' memories, so long as the host can overpower them.

The Foundation recovers the SCP from a GOI (likely MC&D) after someone in the GOI unwittingly flicked it on while alive, causing the user to take the previous user’s consciousness and turn into a human with two minds, with two separate consciousnesses and all of its memories and skills. The GOI then used this to its own advantage, killing targets and employees with high levels of skill/competence/important memories and then adding them to some central source (becoming a sort of librarian/bookkeeper of minds). The bookkeeper is then interviewed by the Foundation, in which the Foundation attempts to loosen the bookkeeper’s mental strength in order to interview some of the other consciousnesses trapped within. Forcing a corpse/non-organic material to switch it off has no effect.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Keeping it short and simple, with an addendum explaining the GOI’s usage and recovery notes.

Additional Notes: I imagine the article itself will be brief (here is a lightswitch, it turns people on and off, no testing allowed, etc) with an addendum that holds the real meat of the SCP (recovery, interview).

In the interview, the Bookkeeper explains that he is the third iteration of them, and continuously absorbs the previous one before him. He mentions that plans were in place to try and create a sort of “generational immortality”, although they didn’t get very far.

6. Envy (Person with something youve always wanted, they leave it out of their sight, working on something)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The 7 deadly sins, all leading to the roof. Must be some reward.

item.content:encoded:

Genre: Bits of Horror and Action.

Elevator Pitch: The basic idea is that a large humanoid creature is found accompanied with a feline in which they seemed to hold a link where the former guards the latter in an overprotective style.

This meaning that anything that draws close to the cat would be considered a potential threat if it was the first time encountering one another and multiple, timed sessions would need to be implemented before the human comes off its high guard.

However both appear to harness a certain weakness to nature so wood, fruit or vegetables would render them either weakened or agitated depending on the dosage provided at that time making it a good counter measure during a containment breach if used properly.

The level of understanding held by both specimens could be exploited by persuading them into helping the facility when keeping other SCPs secured or when cross testing to give varying results due to how differently the two may react in different situations.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The two would originally be found within a town after multiple disappearance are reported only for a task force to discover the hideout of the anomalies until they come to a conclusion that suits the both of them. After being contained in their new home they seem relatively fine with their living arrangements but soon begin asking for more things in exchange for doing tasks or participating in cross testing procedures when being asked about it.

This would lead to contained cross testing between different SCPs of the human's capabilities once in an enraged form after the cat is removed from the select distance previously set up whilst cross testing the cat with safe class human SCPs to see if progress can be made with them in any way. This raising talk of weaponizing the humanoid.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The bond between the two being demonstrated only to be used by the foundation to create a weapon out of the humanoid creating a blackmail scenario where it tries to be with its cat once again whilst remaining within the rules it agreed to. Not to mention, the diverse between understanding and blind rage it has to swap constantly between if it doesn't want to risk being terminated by either the SCPs or the scientists that have it under lock and key.

item.title: Accessible Issue
item.description: I’m sure this seems stupid to old veterans, but Id like to be heard out
item.content:encoded:
Hello,

So the SCP Foundation is an incredible premise that can create some unique stories based on it’s premise alone. That being said, as someone who has now made multiple attempts at SCP’s I’d like to talk about some issues I see in the sight as an outsider.

+ Greenlight Troubles
- Greenlight Troubles

The site’s process for creating new SCPs, especially for new creators, is close focused at best. The fictional Foundation is supposed to be a clinical world facing fantastical elements, but as someone coming in, the similarities to the real site are a bit unnerving. To say nothing of the users, from personal experience they are fine, and sometimes friendly, this is purely about how a brand new author. To give credit, yes an author can develop ideas outside the site plenty, but that doesn't change they then have to convince at least two reviewers in a small paragraph there idea is worth it. Not impossible, obviously, but a little convoluted. I think the ability for more freedom in trying to convey what makes an idea worth it could benefit this site greatly. Once again: this spot isn’t impossible, but cam present real problems to someone in trying to cram an idea into a small format.

+ Aaaand its gone
- Aaaand its gone

The rating system means with -10 likes, a page meets the criteria for deletion. Now again, I can appreciate the benefits of running a strict site, but something about this seems a little cruel. For a site requiring hard work from new creators, all it takes is ten people deciding to press a button saying they didn’t like it, and that says to the author this page is worthy of deletion. It could be absolutely certain that if every site had a shallow enough criteria, many beloved posts would be gone before they blew up. Im not saying enough downvotes isn’t indicative of a post possibly needing deletion, but maybe that particular field needs to be stretched, and authors in general given a chance. After all theres no way to actually know if the majority of site users dislike an SCP, the votes are only indicative of the people who found that page.

+ Slightly Personal
- slightly personal

Once again, I’m sure to some this seems like the ravings of a writer who was a little hurt, and in some part I give credit that it does come from that. More so though, I’d argue that this is also the perspective of someone who has worked hard to try and join really creative people, and been turned away not necessarily by them, but by a system coming across as super insular. It occurs to me maybe I’m also ridiculous for trying to join a catalogue cresting the 6000’s, but under the impression that this universe could be even more I did wanna try. Definitely some fault is mine in writing, lets not pretend any old SCP’s I made would be the next 096, but my point lies in that: in trying to add to something I’ve seen as fun and a little silly, I’ve been met with an incredibly high wall, in some ways earned by the site, but in many ways just as ridiculous.

In closing: the site’s a little too insular. This doesn’t necessarily warrant a whole overhaul, but maybe a reflective look at how some things should be run. I suppose if you want to write this off as a newbee venting, thats fine, but I think it would great benefit the Foundation to genuinely look at how it handles new ideas, and what kind of criteria it has, and whether or not its always fair.
